sentences.text: 1 2. The prayer is not opposed by the learned counsel for the respondent No.3/ Insurance Company.

3. After due consideration and taking note of the fact that respondents No.1 and 2, driver and owner of the offending vehicle respectively were ex- parte before the Tribunal; therefore, the service on respondent No.2 is hereby dispensed with.

4. The instant Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 7.04.2014 passed in Claim Case No.133/2012 by 10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior, whereby the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,10,600/- in favour of appellant/claimant along with interest @ 7.5% per annum.

5. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal in brief are that on 12.2.2012 at about 1:00 A.M. appellant Rajendra @ Raju was going to Jagrati Nagar with his uncle Kamlesh Rathore by motorcycle.

When they reached near Laxmiganj Chouraha A.B. Road, at that time one truck bearing registration NO.HR.55-P-6746 which was being driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently dashed the motorcycle, due to which, appellant sustained grievous injuries in left leg, left hand and other parts of the body.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant have sustained two fractures in tibia fibula bone and left radius but learned tribunal has awarded the amount of compensation on lower side.

Having regard to the nature of the injury sustained by the appellant Rs.50,000/- on the head of fractures ought to be allowed by the learned Tribunal and on the other hand compensation may be enhanced.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel of the Insurance Company opposed the prayer on the ground that appropriate award has been passed in favour of the claimants/appellants and there is no ground for enhancement of the award and it has been prayed that the appeal may be dismissed.
8. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the record, it is found that two fractures have been sustained by the appellant in the accident.
Learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- on the head of pain and suffering which ought to be enhanced upto Rs.50,000/-.
On the head of special diet and attender expenses, the amount awarded also needs to be enhanced.

The appellant was under treatment from February to May, therefore, three months loss of earning is on the lower side and it ought to be 4 months loss of earning; therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record Rs.35,000/- may be appropriate to be enhanced in favour of the appellant/claimant.
9.
In the result, Rs.35,000/- is hereby enhanced in favour of the appellant in addition to the award already passed in his favour.
The remaining terms and conditions as stipulated in the impugned award shall remain intact.
1 0 . With the aforesaid observation, the Miscellaneous Appeal is disposed off.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Ahmad Rajendra @ Raju vs Arsad on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95586369/
